newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: US again seeking a seat on UN budget committee.
newsitem.headline: US again seeking a seat on UN budget committee.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador Bill Richardson suggested on Tuesday enlarging the membership of a key U.N. budget committee to accomodate the United States, which was thrown off the panel last November.
Known as the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, or ACABQ, the 16-member panel plays a crucial role in reviewing the U.N.'s $1.3 billion annual budget.
Richardson, in speaking to a General Assembly of U.N. ambassadors analysing the U.N. system, said that "expanding the ACABQ membership bears our consideration."
"We will be consulting with colleagues on this point," he added.

In a suprise move on Nov. 9, France and New Zealand won election over the United States in a fairly close vote, mainly because of anger at the more than $1 billion U.S. debt to the world body. It was the first time that Washington did not get a place on the panel of financial experts.
Western diplomats at the time said the United States would probably regain its seat late in 1997 and thought the vote reflected momentary pique at American failure to pay its arrears.

Another factor, they said, was the unpopularity of Minister-Counsellor Linda Shenwick, the U.S. delegate who had served on the panel for years and who has close ties to conservative Republicans. She was to be replaced by Melinda Kimble who was not well known and had done little campaigning.
